 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Italy are expected to start Pio Esposito, Sandro Tonali, Riccardo Calafiori and Michael Kayode in the penultimate Nations League match, while France rely on Michael Olise in the absence of Kylian Mbappé.
 It kicks off at San Siro, the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza in Milan, on Thursday at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Only the top two go through from Group A1 into the quarter-finals of the Nations League, and currently France lead on 10 points, followed by Italy with seven and Belgium on six.
 The final round will see the Azzurri and Red Devils go head-to-head in Brussels, while France host rock bottom Turkiye.
 BOLOGNA – OCTOBER 05: Roberto Mancini, Manager of Italy, reacts during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Italy and Türkiye at Renato Dall'Ara Stadium on October 05, 2026 in Bologna. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)
 Roberto Mancini is expected to adopt his usual 4-3-3 formation, but there are quite a few doubts over the starting XI. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Brentford right-back Kayode would seem to have done enough to earn his spot, while Arsenal's Calafiori at left-back means dropping Inter man Federico Dimarco to the bench.
 An alternative would be moving Calafiori to central defence with Alessandro Bastoni, therefore starting Dimarco and sending Giorgio Scalvini to the touchline.
 BURSA, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 28: Michael Kayode of Italy celebrates scoring his team's third goal with teammate Sandro Tonali during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Türkiye and Italy at Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matli Stadyumu on September 28, 2026 in Bursa, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images)
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In midfield, Davide Frattesi and Tonali seem sure of their places, with Nicolò Barella of Inter the favourite to complete the trio.
 Inter striker Pio Esposito is set to lead the attack, but the rest of the trident is up in the air.
 His older brother Sebastiano Esposito is the primary candidate on the right side ahead of Como's Mattia Liberali, while Nicolò Cambiaghi of Bologna would seem to be ahead of Luca Koleosho on the left.
 France coach Zinedine Zidane on the touchline during the Nations League match with Italy in Paris (@equipedefrance)
 France go into this match without Real Madrid striker Mbappé due to a hamstring injury, and curiously he was also absent when these two teams drew 1-1 in Paris on October 2. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement He isn't the only one, as they have had to give up on Marcus Thuram, Pierre Kalulu, Aurelien Tchouameni, Manu Koné, William Saliba, Jules Koundé, Maxence Lacroix, Ousmane Dembélé, Maghnes Akliouche and Esteban Lepaul.
 It is therefore likely that the front three will be made up of Olise, Désiré Doué and Bradley Barcola, but in which order remains to be seen.
 Barcola was not originally included to be a centre-forward, but might have to adapt in the circumstances.
 BRUSSELS, BELGIUM – SEPTEMBER 28: Kevin De Bruyne of Belgium shoots under pressure from Bradley Barcola of France during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Belgium and France at Stade Roi Baudouin on September 28, 2026 in Brussels, Belgium. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images)
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement If not, then Eli Junior Kroupi or 20-year-old late addition Senny Mayulu could be wild card alternatives to start as Number 9.
 There is Serie A representation from Milan pair Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot, while Como midfielder Lucas Da Cunha is expected to start, although Eduardo Camavinga is waiting in the wings.
 In defence, Adrien Truffert of Bournemouth is the favourite over Inter's Andy Diouf for left-back, with either Ibrahim Konaté or Jérémy Jacquet in central defence.
 PARIS, FRANCE – OCTOBER 02: Rayan Cherki of France reacts alongside teammate Adrien Rabiot before the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between France and Italy at Stade de France on October 02, 2026 in Paris, France. (Photo by Pauline Figuet/Getty Images)
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Italy vs. France probable line-ups
 Italy (4-3-3): Donnarumma; Kayode, Scalvini, Bastoni, Calafiori; Frattesi, Tonali, Barella; S Esposito, Pio Esposito, Cambiaghi
 France (4-3-3): Maignan; Gusto, Konaté, Upamecano, Truffert; Cherki, Da Cunha, Rabiot; Olise, Barcola, Doué
